_README: Shared narrative contract. Golden vectors keep the NUMBERS in lockstep between a still figure and its interactive; this file keeps the WORDS in lockstep. Every caption, caveat and on-screen distortion statement that must appear in more than one artifact lives here and is read by both the Python figure scripts and the HTML builders. Added after the boundary-condition caveat was fixed in twin_panel.py and shipped missing from twin_scrubber.html. See DISTORTION_LEDGER.md, standing entry on propagation.

alpha4a.boundary_condition: u is the solution that DECAYS as Y -> +infinity. The escape problem picks that one. A different boundary condition (Bi, or a mixture) has different zeros - so these are not "the" zeros, they are this condition's zeros.
alpha4a.boundary_condition_html: u is the solution that decays as Y → +∞ — the escape problem picks that one. A different boundary condition has different zeros, so these are not “the” zeros, they are this condition’s zeros.
alpha4a.the_trade: blow-ups are hard to see. zeros are easy. Cole-Hopf buys you zeros.
alpha4a.not_tw: not the scaling limit - this is not TW

alpha3.headline: Blow-up is anisotropic zoom.
alpha3.naive_fails: Zoom in on the fold with both axes magnified equally and the critical manifold flattens toward a straight line. Every zoom level looks the same and shows less. The tool fails.
alpha3.the_find: Magnify y as the SQUARE of x and the parabola stops moving. It is now invariant under zoom. That exponent - weight 2 on y against weight 1 on x - is the blow-up weight, and you found it by feel rather than by being told.
alpha3.third_weight: The manifold is not the whole picture. Turn the trajectory on and it still drifts, because the slow parameter eps carries a weight of its own. Give it weight 3 and the trajectory settles too.
alpha3.the_real_point: Watch the equation, not the picture. Every lambda in it carries an exponent built from the weights you chose. At p=2 and q=3 both exponents hit zero and lambda DISAPPEARS FROM THE EQUATION. That is what a blow-up is for: not a nicer picture, but a system that no longer knows how far in you zoomed.
alpha3.what_it_is: The charts K1/K2/K3 are which face of that zoom you look through, and the exceptional divisor is the set of approach directions the naive zoom collapses to a single point.
alpha3.payoff: The lambda-free equation you are left with is X' = X^2 - Y, Y' = -eps. That is the inner Riccati - the same equation whose blow-ups you traded for zeros in the previous module.
alpha3.distortion_not_added: Nothing is being ADDED to the space. The blow-down map is a diffeomorphism away from the origin; this is the same neighbourhood seen through a distorting lens, not new geometry.
alpha3.distortion_no_sphere: The sphere of the usual construction is not drawn. This is one chart. Opening on the sphere is the standard way this topic loses people.

alpha4c.headline: Shooting: the zeros are the spectrum.
alpha4c.setup: The operator is H = -d²/dx² + x on the half-line, with u(0) = 0. Pick a trial energy lambda, start from the decaying end, and integrate back to the wall at x = 0. Almost always you miss.
alpha4c.the_miss: u(0) is the miss. Slide lambda and watch it. Where the miss crosses zero you have an eigenvalue - and at that instant a new node appears in u. That is not a coincidence, it is the oscillation theorem: the n-th eigenfunction has exactly n-1 interior zeros.
alpha4c.the_join: The eigenvalues you are landing on are the Airy zeros, |a_n| = 2.338, 4.088, 5.521, ... - the same numbers that marked the crossings of u and the blow-ups of R two modules ago. The escape levels and the spectrum are one set of numbers counted twice.
alpha4c.distortion_scale: u is normalised for display. An eigenfunction is defined only up to scale, so the height carries no meaning - only the zeros and the sign of the miss do.
alpha4c.distortion_halfline: The wall at x = 0 with u(0) = 0 is a boundary condition imposed to make the spectrum discrete. On the whole line the Airy operator has no eigenvalues at all; the escape problem is what puts the wall there.

gamma8.headline: Stokes phenomenon: the jump that isn't a jump.
gamma8.setup: Rotate around the Airy function in the complex plane. Its asymptotic expansion has two exponentials, e^-zeta and e^+zeta, and which one you are allowed to ignore depends on where you stand. The coefficient of the ignorable one is the Stokes multiplier.
gamma8.textbook: The textbook picture says the multiplier is 0 on one side of a Stokes line and S0 on the other - a step. That picture is wrong at every finite radius.
gamma8.berry: Berry's result: the switching is SMOOTH, and universally so. Across the line the multiplier follows an error function in sigma = Im(zeta)/sqrt(2 Re zeta), with an angular width of order |zeta|^-1/2. Push the radius out and the ramp sharpens toward a step - which is why the step is drawn, and why it is only ever a limit.
gamma8.what_switches: Nothing discontinuous happens to the function. Ai(z) is entire - it has no jumps anywhere. What jumps is our DESCRIPTION of it: a term we were entitled to drop becomes a term we are not. The Stokes line is a fact about the asymptotic representation, not about the function.
gamma8.constant: The Stokes constant for the Airy equation is exactly i. It is fixed by the connection identity Ai(z) + w*Ai(wz) + w_bar*Ai(w_bar z) = 0 with w = exp(2*pi*i/3), which holds identically - verified numerically to machine precision in the build.
gamma8.distortion_convention: Convention warning: some authors call Im(zeta)=0 the Stokes lines (used here, following Berry), others reserve that name for Re(zeta)=0. Reading across sources without checking which is meant is a reliable way to get the geometry backwards.
gamma8.distortion_erf: The error-function profile is the leading term of Berry's smoothing, not an exact evaluation of the multiplier. It is asymptotic in |zeta|, so it is least trustworthy exactly where it is most visible - at small radius, where the ramp is broadest.

delta1.headline: The junction: one ladder, built by geometry, read by analysis.
delta1.setup: Everything geometric in this course produces one sequence of numbers. Everything analytic consumes it. This is where the two halves touch, and they touch at a single quantity: the instanton action.
delta1.geometry_side: Hold the escape off to depth s and the cheapest way to do it costs I(s) = (1/2) integral of p^2, with p = t^q along the way. That integral is elementary: I(s) = s^(2q+1) / [2(2q+1)]. Nothing asymptotic, nothing fitted - just an area.
delta1.analysis_side: That same number does two jobs on the other side. It sets the tail, P(depth > s) ~ exp(-I/eta^2). And it sets where the Borel singularity sits, so it fixes how fast the coefficients v_k diverge. Geometry hands analysis a number; the divergence rate hands it back.
delta1.the_family: Change the rung and only the exponent moves: 2q+1 runs 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 for fold, cusp, swallowtail and beyond. One formula, five rungs. That is the ladder.
delta1.distortion_factor2: This constant was wrong in this project's own notes for a while. An earlier draft carried I(s) = s^(2q+1)/[4(2q+1)] - too small by a factor of 2 - until the q=2 case was checked against a boundary-value solve and disagreed. The formula shown here is the corrected one.
delta1.distortion_leading: p = t^q is the leading behaviour of the optimal path, not the path itself. The closed form is the leading-order action; a boundary-value solve of the full Euler-Lagrange system approaches it from below, and at fixed s the low rungs are still visibly short of it.
delta1.distortion_onerung: The coefficient ladder shown is the cusp, q=2, which is settled and published. The swallowtail ladder is still being refined at the top rungs and is deliberately not drawn here.
delta1.ratio_setup: Now the other half. If a single singularity sat on the positive real axis at distance A, the ratios of successive Borel coefficients would settle down to 1/A. That is the standard way to read a singularity off a series.
delta1.ratio_finding: They do not settle. They swing - sign flip at k=2, a spike above 3.7 at k=3, then back down. That is not noise and it is not a failure of the engine: it is what a COMPLEX CONJUGATE PAIR does. A pair at modulus 1.9 and angle 50 degrees reproduces the whole sequence to half a percent, with one fitted phase.
delta1.ratio_limit: But the modulus is not readable from seven coefficients. The root test gives 2.5-2.7 against a true value near 1.9 and is not converging. So the coefficients DO know the geometry - the swing encodes the angle, the envelope the modulus - and seven of them are not enough to read it off naively. That is precisely why this programme needed a matched-truncation calibration rather than a textbook Domb-Sykes.

delta3.headline: Three families, one word
delta3.setup: "Multicritical" names at least three different objects in this literature, and the differences are not cosmetic — two of the three are integrable by construction and one is provably not. This module is the coda: it exists so the ladder you have just climbed is not filed under the wrong heading.
delta3.swept: SWEPT MULTICRITICAL — the family of this course. A second-order operator whose swept turning potential is multicritical. The index q is the turning order. Skeleton: Bessel of order 1/(q+2); the escape levels are its zeros. Provably NOT integrable: no Fredholm/soft-edge determinant (the operator is unbounded below) and no Painlevé σ-reduction (the skeleton is an isomonodromy fixed point).
delta3.genuine: GENUINE DIFFRACTION CATASTROPHE (Berry–Upstill) — an n-th ORDER equation. Airy, then Pearcey, then the swallowtail function. The multicriticality lives in the order of the equation, not in a swept potential. Shares its first rung with us and nothing after.
delta3.rmt: RANDOM-MATRIX MULTICRITICAL EDGE — "higher-order analogues of Tracy–Widom". When the equilibrium density vanishes to higher order at the edge, the limit laws are Fredholm determinants of higher Airy-type kernels from the Painlevé I/II hierarchies. Integrable by construction. This is the family whose name collides with ours most dangerously.
delta3.divergence: The two ODE families agree at the fold and then move in OPPOSITE directions. As the swept turning order q rises the laws grow MORE skewed; as the Berry–Upstill order n rises they trend TOWARD Gaussian. One shared rung is not a shared family.
delta3.falsify: If these were one family, the two curves would track each other instead of separating after their shared first rung — and the swept rungs would inherit an integrable structure. Neither happens.
delta3.distortion_slice: Any swallowtail SURFACE that can be drawn is a slice of a higher-dimensional unfolding, and it belongs to family 2, not to this course's family 1. It is shown here only to name the object being distinguished — never as the thing the ladder is made of.
delta3.distortion_thirdcol: The third column has no coefficient ladder drawn beside the others because it is not built the same way: it is a limit law of an ensemble, not the first-passage law of a swept operator. Placing three columns side by side implies a common construction that does not exist; only the WORD is common.
delta3.distortion_skew: The skew values are measured, not derived — Monte-Carlo for the swept rungs (2.8e6 escapes each) and numerical integration for the Berry–Upstill ones. They carry sampling error of order the last digit shown, which is far below the separation being claimed but is not zero.

ep0.headline: A neuron fires. The timing is random. The randomness has a shape.
ep0.setup: This is FitzHugh-Nagumo with a little noise on the voltage - about the simplest thing that spikes. Let it run. The spikes are not evenly spaced, and the gaps between them are not spread out evenly either: the histogram builds a definite, lopsided shape.
ep0.q1: QUESTION ONE, for the geometry. What is it about the shape of this system that makes a spike happen at all - and what decides WHERE, in the slow drift, the escape occurs?
ep0.q2: QUESTION TWO, for the analysis. Why THAT shape? A lopsided distribution with a sharp edge on one side and a long tail on the other is not what you would guess. Where does its form come from?
ep0.promise: Those two questions run as separate threads and stay separate for a long time. They meet once, at a single sequence of numbers, and the answer to the second turns out to be a law that does not care which neuron model you started from.
ep0.distortion_notreal: This is a reduced model, not a neuron. FitzHugh-Nagumo throws away ion channels, spatial structure and most biophysics; it keeps two timescales and a cubic nonlinearity. The claim of this course is about that geometry, not about cells.
ep0.distortion_isi: The histogram is of inter-spike intervals from one long run at fixed parameters. It is not the escape law the course derives - that one is a distribution over the ESCAPE POINT in the slow variable, which is related but not identical.

alpha12.headline: Fast, slow, and the place it breaks.
alpha12.setup: Two timescales. The voltage moves fast, the recovery variable slowly. Turn the separation up and the trajectory stops looking like a curve and starts looking like a circuit: crawl, jump, crawl, jump.
alpha12.manifold: The crawling happens on the critical manifold - the cubic curve where the fast direction is at rest. The jumps happen where that curve folds back on itself. Everything interesting in this course happens at those two fold points.
alpha12.attraction: Why the jump? Because the manifold is only ATTRACTING where the fast direction pulls you back onto it, and the strength of that pull is 1 - v². It is strong in the middle of a branch and it goes to ZERO at the fold.
alpha12.breakdown: That is the failure. Fenichel's theorem - the result that guarantees the slow manifold survives the perturbation at all - needs the attraction to be bounded away from zero. At the fold it is not, so the theorem does not apply, the slow-fast splitting stops being a description, and every tool built on it stops working. The whole next module exists because of this one number going to zero.
alpha12.distortion_planar: Planar FHN only. In higher dimensions folded singularities have more structure (folded nodes, folded saddles) and the story branches; nothing here shows that.
alpha12.distortion_rate: 1 - v² is the linear attraction rate at the manifold, i.e. the eigenvalue of the fast subsystem. Calling it 'the strength of the pull' is a fair gloss for a rate, but it is a rate.

gamma1.headline: A series that gets worse the more of it you use.
gamma1.setup: Here is a perfectly ordinary-looking function with a perfectly ordinary-looking power series: E(x) = integral of e^-t/(1+xt), whose expansion is the alternating sum of k! x^k. The function is exactly computable, so for once we can watch the series against the truth.
gamma1.the_shock: Add terms and the error falls, which is what you expect. Keep adding and it RISES. There is a best number of terms, and past it every extra term makes the answer worse. The series does not converge for any x at all - its radius of convergence is zero.
gamma1.the_floor: The best you can do is the size of the smallest term, and that floor is not a power of x: it goes like e^(-1/x). An exponential has appeared out of a pure power series, and no finite part of that series can see it.
gamma1.the_hook: So a divergent series is not useless and it is not merely bad - it has a definite accuracy limit, and the limit is exponentially small. Everything in the analysis thread of this course is about what lives underneath that floor and how to get at it.
gamma1.distortion_alternating: This series alternates, which makes it the EASY case - it is Borel summable with no ambiguity. The series this course actually cares about does not alternate, and that difference is exactly where the trouble starts.
gamma1.distortion_optimal: Truncating at the least term is a rule of thumb, not a theorem. It is very good here and it is the standard practice, but the optimal truncation point and the error at it are asymptotic statements.

alpha5.headline: The same law, arriving from somewhere else entirely.
alpha5.setup: Take a large random Hermitian matrix. Its eigenvalues fill a semicircle. Look only at the LARGEST one: it sits near the edge, and it jitters from one matrix to the next. That jitter is the whole subject here.
alpha5.raw: Drawn as they come, the distributions for different matrix sizes look nothing alike - the bigger the matrix, the tighter the largest eigenvalue clamps to the edge. There is no common shape to see.
alpha5.collapse: Now rescale: measure the gap to the edge in units of N^(-2/3). Every size collapses onto ONE curve. The shape does not depend on N, and it does not depend on the details of the matrix either. That is what universality means, and the collapse is the mechanism - not slow convergence but a fixed shape hiding behind a shrinking scale.
alpha5.reveal: That curve is the Tracy-Widom distribution. And it is the law this course has been circling from the other side: the escape statistics of a noisy neuron at a fold. A random matrix and a spiking cell have no business sharing a distribution, and they share this one.
alpha5.why: The bridge is the stochastic Airy operator. The edge of the spectrum and the escape problem both reduce to the ground state of -d^2/dx^2 + x + noise, so they are not analogous - they are the same computation wearing different clothes.
alpha5.distortion_beta2: GUE only, i.e. beta=2. The fold problem's law is TW_beta with beta set by the noise strength, and beta=2 is one slice of it. Nothing here varies beta.
alpha5.distortion_cited: The identification with the escape problem is CITED, not derived here - it rests on the Ramirez-Rider-Virag theorem. This module shows the random-matrix side is Tracy-Widom; it does not re-derive the neuron side.
alpha5.distortion_finite: These are finite matrices with finite samples. The collapse is excellent by N=25, which is a real and slightly surprising fact, but the limit statement is asymptotic and the histograms carry sampling noise - visible in the skew, which is far noisier than the mean or the width.

delta2.headline: Up the ladder, the structure survives and the solvability does not.
delta2.setup: Every rung is the same problem with a higher-order turning point: the potential goes like Y^q instead of Y. Fold, cusp, swallowtail, and onward. The question is what carries over.
delta2.skeleton: The skeleton carries over exactly. Solve u'' = Y^q u and the answer is a Bessel function of order 1/(q+2) - one third at the fold, one quarter at the cusp, one fifth at the swallowtail. Verified here against direct integration at six rungs to ten decimal places. The family is real and it is not a coincidence of the first two.
delta2.degrade: What does NOT carry over is solvability. At the fold the connection problem is Airy and the answer is exact. At the cusp it is Weber, still closed-form, still Gamma-type. At the swallowtail it is the cubic oscillator: exactly characterised by a T-Q system, and NOT of Gamma-type - so there is no closed phase to compare against. Structure persists; closed forms run out.
delta2.refuge: That is why resurgence is not a stylistic preference here. Above the cusp there is no Painleve reduction to fall back on and no Fredholm determinant to write down, so the trans-series is not one representation among several - it is the only one available. The divergent series stops being an embarrassment and becomes the definition.
delta2.distortion_dlmf: The special functions themselves are not replotted here. DLMF chapter 36.3, by Berry and Howls, already does that better than this project would - rotatable, in modulus and phase, across parameter slices. What is added here is the narrative, not the surfaces.
delta2.distortion_absence: 'No Painleve reduction above the cusp' is an absence of a known reduction, plus explicit exclusion results at q=3. It is not a proof that none can exist for every higher rung.
delta2.distortion_notthom: These rungs are indexed by turning ORDER in a second-order equation. They are not Thom's A_k catastrophe surfaces, and the resemblance of the names is a trap - see the coda.
